newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesian rupiah firms in dull late trading.
newsitem.headline: Indonesian rupiah firms in dull late trading.

text.p: The Indonesian rupiah firmed against the dollar in late trading on Monday, dealers said.
They said overall volume was thin on lack of fresh leads.
"There was no drive in the market. The rate was hovering in such a narrow range that it's difficult to make profits," one Japanese bank dealer said.
Spot rupiah was at 2,318.0/19.0 at 0845 GMT, compared with an opening of 2,319.0/20.0.
Dealers said liquidity was ample in the afternoon, but the tom/next swap rate edged up.
The Japanese dealer said it might be due to speculation of tight liquidity on Tuesday for weekly tax payments.
"But I don't think liquidity would be tight because the central bank has offered one to three-day overnight papers (SBIs) to the market," he said.
He said this should help stabilise Tuesday's rupiah market.
Dealers said sentiment on the rupiah remained strong and expected the currency to trade at the central bank's ceiling.
Another foreign bank dealer said the dollar-rupiah rate was expected to range between 2,318 and 2,320 on Tuesday.
Tomorrow and today rupiah closed at 2,317.5/18.0 and 2,318.5/19.0, respectively.
Dealers said longer-term swap rates eased slightly on the back of relatively ample liquidity in the money market.
Overnight money was last at 9.5 percent.
One-month swap was last at 14.75/15.25, two at 30.25/31.00, three at 46.75/47.00 and six at 95.00/96.50 points.
Bank Indonesia raised its intervention rate by one point to 2,313/2,505 and the conversion rate also by one point to 2,313/2,361 on Monday.
